_about: How a Japanese reader would most likely pronounce each kanji when reading it ALOUD ON ITS OWN - on a sign, a headline, a book cover. This is not the same as 'the first reading in the dictionary', and it is not what the kanji is read as inside a compound word.
_why: Deriving this from KANJIDIC2 alone gets it wrong roughly one time in five across the most frequent kanji: the plain heuristic (prefer a kun reading with no okurigana) reads the numerals as 十=とお, 三=み, 九=ここの, and produces 本=もと, 円=まる, 千=ち, 業=わざ. Those are real readings but not what anyone says looking at the bare character. So the frequent range - the range a beginner's first batches actually cover - is curated by hand here, and everything else falls back to the heuristic in app.js.
_howto: This file is data, not code: edit it freely and restart the app. Keys are single kanji, values are the standalone reading in hiragana. Delete an entry to fall back to the heuristic. The app labels each reading on-yomi or kun-yomi automatically by looking it up in kanji.json, and it still accepts the kanji's other readings as correct - the curated one is simply the one it teaches.
_your_own_edits: Updating the app REPLACES this file. To keep your own changes, put them in userdata/spoken.local.json instead - same shape ({"overrides": {...}}), it wins over this file, and everything under userdata/ is out of reach of updates. That file is optional; the app works fine without it.
_caveat: Some entries are genuine judgment calls where two answers are both defensible (後 = のち or あと; 度 = ど or たび; 側 = かわ or がわ). Where that is true, the app accepts both and teaches the one listed here.
